Exercise: Sled Push

Category:
strongman

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- push

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- chest
- glutes
- hamstrings
- triceps

Equipment:

- other

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- hypertrophy
- power
- strength

Contraindications:

- Shoulder instability or injury
- Lower back pain or injury

Exercise Variations:

- name: Sled Pull, force: pull, level: beginner
- name: Barbell Push-Up, force: push, level: beginner

Substitution Options:

- name: Barbell Push Press, force: push, level: intermediate
- name: Kettlebell Clean and Press, force: push, level: intermediate

Instructions:

- Load your pushing sled with the desired weight.
- Take an athletic posture, leaning into the sled with your arms fully extended, grasping the handles. Push the sled as fast as possible, focusing on extending your hips and knees to strengthen your posterior chain.
